residual_risk: The concurrency test is deterministic injection, not a real race: every git call here is spawnSync, so two commit() calls cannot interleave inside one process. The interfering write is made from a second GitTier inside the mutation callback — exactly where the race window is, between the read and the update-ref — which guarantees the CAS refusal and the retry replay are exercised. A two-process race was not staged; it would be timing-dependent and flakier for no extra coverage. A reviewer wanting it should run two `node -e` children in a loop against one scratch repo.

`test/store.test.js` was NOT edited, so the card's 'register the driver in DRIVERS' checkbox is answered differently than written: the durable scenarios are duplicated into test/store-git.test.js instead. Reason: DRIVERS holds whole Stores and the shape check (STORE_METHODS) would fail a tier that deliberately has no locks or events, and test/store.test.js is outside this node's `paths` while A5 runs beside it. The cost is real — the two scenario lists can now drift. A6 should delete the duplicated block when src/store/local.js joins DRIVERS.

Notes have no path of their own on the branch. §6.2 names board.json, cards/ and runs/ and nothing else, and §6.3's index has a `notes` table, so human notes were put inside runs/<id>.json. If A5/A6 decide notes deserve `notes/<id>.json`, this is the file to change and the migration is mechanical — but it is a layout choice this card made, not one the plan states.

`url` is always null and `prs` always empty on a task from this tier. A local board has no issue URL, and pull requests are src/forge.js's. Any caller that renders task.url without a guard will print `null`; the GitHub store always fills it. A6 should decide whether the composed store synthesizes one.

`board()` reads the whole tree to answer, and every verb does a full readTree() before and a getTask() after. That is two to three git chains per write where the GitHub store did one request. It is correct and it is fast on a board of this size, but there is no caching layer here on purpose — the index (A5) is the read cache, and A6 composing them is what makes reads cheap. Do not add a cache to this file.

`git update-index --add --index-info` and `git hash-object -w -t blob --stdin-paths` were verified working on the git in this environment; both are long-standing plumbing, but the CI matrix (Node 22/24/26) does not pin a git version and neither flag combination is exercised anywhere else in the repo.

isContended() classifies a CAS refusal by matching git's message text ('cannot lock ref', 'is at X but expected Y', 'reference already exists'). A future git that rewords those would turn a contended write into a hard exit-2 failure rather than a retry — noisy and safe, not silent, but it is a string match.

results.summary: src/store/git.js is the durable tier of a local board: board.json, cards/<id>.json and runs/<id>.json on refs/heads/kb-board, written with plumbing only. A read is one `ls-tree -r` plus one `cat-file --batch` (two processes for a board of any size, never one per file); the read returns every blob's sha, so a write only hashes the files whose bytes changed. A write is one chain — `hash-object -w --stdin-paths`, `update-index --index-info` against a scratch GIT_INDEX_FILE, `write-tree`, `commit-tree`, `update-ref <new> <expected-old>` — with no checkout, no staging and no working-tree write anywhere in the module (a test asserts that against the source). update-ref IS the compare-and-swap: a refusal re-reads and REPLAYS the mutation callback on the newer tree, up to 5 times, then exit 2 naming the owning host. That is why commit() takes a callback and not a diff — a mutation that closes over state read before commit() breaks the retry. A write whose bytes are unchanged lands no commit. board.json names one owning host and every write refuses on any other naming `hkb init --take-over` (takeOver() moves it); a clone with no local branch falls back to refs/remotes/origin/kb-board and reads. Ids are integers from board.json.next_id. Files are sorted-key, two-space JSON with one trailing newline. All git runs at storeRoot(ctx) with GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_INDEX_FILE and friends unset. FOR THE NEXT NODE (A6): this is a TIER, not a Store — it has none of claim/release/listLocks/lockBeatAt/heartbeat/events, and a scenario asserts their absence, so compose it with A5's index in src/store/local.js and register THAT in test/store.test.js's DRIVERS. Every method is SYNCHRONOUS (spawnSync throughout) and returns a value, not a promise; awaiting them is harmless, but a caller relying on async interleaving between two store calls gets none. openGitTier(ctx, {ref, remote, host, now}) and `new GitTier(pathOrCtx, opts)` both work. Card records hoist priority/paths/goal/scheduled_at as §6.2 shows and keep every other kb key under a `kb` object on the same file; labels that are not columns (kb:no-track, a human's own) ride in a `labels` array. Notes and parsed results live in runs/<id>.json alongside the attempts — §6.2 does not name a notes path, and addNote() routes a RESULT_MARKER body into `results` (which latestResult reads) and refuses a RUN_MARKER body with exit 2 pointing at saveRun.
